To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

women in abusive relationships who are also at high risk for HIV are at high risk for engaging in sexual risk behavior and that the risk for HIV infection among this population can be reduced through the implementation of a culturally competent intervention.

women who were victims of domestic violence and who had HIV risk factors were more likely to be tested and to receive treatment for HIV if they were in a relationship with a man who had been diagnosed with HIV and if the women were in a supportive relationship with a friend or family member.
the intervention was effective in reducing HIV risk behavior and in improving women’s knowledge of HIV risk.

the development of an HIV/AIDS prevention intervention for low income women with histories of intimate partner violence.
the development of an HIV/AIDS prevention intervention for lowincome, battered women.
the design of culturally competent interventions for battered women.

the use of a developmental research approach may be one way to integrate cross cultural practice issues into the process of designing and developing interventions that are culturally sensitive.
this model provides one way of integrating the tasks of cross cultural practice into the first four developmental research phases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developmental research model can provide a useful structure for the design and implementation of culturally competent intervention.
the integration of cross-cultural issues into the phases of developmental intervention design and development can be a useful vehicle for designing and delivering culturally competent interventions.
culturally competent intervention requires that the cultural context of the target population be considered in all aspects of research and intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cultural issues are important in the design and development phases of research.
cultural considerations should be integrated throughout the developmental research process, rather than being relegated to a single step in the research process.
culturally competent practice requires that cultural considerations be integrated into all phases of developmental research.
